sc: Well 3-year-old, smooth flank mass not crossing the midline, haematuria, high BP → Wilms tumour
Ill 18-month-old, hard abdominal mass crossing the midline, raccoon eyes → Neuroblastoma
6-year-old, fast-growing jaw swelling, loose teeth, starry-sky biopsy → Burkitt lymphoma
f: White pupil (retinoblastoma) · unexplained mass · morning headache with vomiting · bone pain at night · node > 2 cm or > 4–6 weeks
Wilms: 3–4 yr, well, smooth, does not cross midline, cure ~90% · neuroblastoma: < 2 yr, ill, crosses midline, urine VMA/HVA, MIBG
Hodgkin: teenager, rubbery nodes, B symptoms, Reed–Sternberg cells · Burkitt: jaw (endemic) or abdomen, very fast, tumour lysis
Medulloblastoma: truncal ataxia · craniopharyngioma: bitemporal hemianopia, short, polyuria · retinoblastoma: RB1, bilateral = heritable
Excision biopsy of a node · ultrasound then CT (chest for Wilms metastases: lungs) · MRI brain · AFP (hepatoblastoma)
Ewing: fever, onion-skin X-ray · osteosarcoma: knee, sunburst
trap: Raccoon eyes in a toddler with an abdominal mass = metastatic neuroblastoma, not abuse · mediastinal mass: keep the child sitting up, no sedation · dancing eyes = opsoclonus–myoclonus (neuroblastoma)
